guide.watch: Each sentence should start with a capital. A comma after First, Then and Next is good practice.

title: Nouns, plurals and tenses Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on nouns, plurals and tenses, from "Common or Proper?" to "Past, Present, Future". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort common and proper nouns.
Write irregular plurals.
Identify past, present and future tense.

guide.what: Common and proper nouns, plurals that break the rules, and verbs in the past, present and future.
steps: Proper nouns are names: ask "Is it a special name?"
Learn tricky plurals as pairs: mouse, mice.
Look for time words: yesterday, now, tomorrow.
home: Find proper nouns in a newspaper and circle the capitals.
Tell a story about yesterday, today and tomorrow.
guide.watch: Children often write "childs" or "mouses". Keep a tricky plurals list on the fridge.

title: Spelling patterns Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on spelling patterns, from "Magic E" to "Sounds of -ed". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read and spell words with a silent e (magic e).
Spell words with silent b and k.
Hear the three sounds of the -ed ending.

guide.what: Spelling patterns: magic e, silent letters and the three sounds of -ed.
steps: Say the word with and without the magic e: cap, cape.
Point out letters we write but do not say.
Say -ed words and listen: is it t, d or id?
home: Write a list of silent letter words found in books.
Play magic e: write a word and let your child add e.
guide.watch: Spelling grows with reading. Children who read daily see patterns many times.

title: Classic poems Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on classic poems, from "Who Has Seen the Wind?" to "Acrostic Poem". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a poem and understand its meaning.
Find adjectives and imagery in a poem.
Write an acrostic poem.

guide.what: Reading classic poems for meaning, noticing describing words, and writing an acrostic poem.
steps: Read the poem aloud twice, slowly.
Ask: What picture does this poem make in your mind?
Underline the describing words.
home: Learn one poem by heart and say it to the family.
Write an acrostic for your name.
guide.watch: Poetry is meant to be felt. Ask "How does this poem make you feel?" as well as "What does it mean?"

title: Main idea and inference Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on main idea and inference, from "The Markhor" to "Road Safety". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Find the main idea of a passage.
Infer feelings and reasons from clues in a text.
Understand character and give reasons.

guide.what: Finding the main idea of a passage and using clues to work out what the writer does not say.
steps: Ask: What is this passage mostly about? Say it in one sentence.
For inference, ask: What clues tell us that?
Answer with a reason: "I think... because..."
home: Watch a short video without sound and guess how people feel.
After a story, ask: Why did the character do that?
guide.watch: Inference is a big step. Model it: "Ammi's eyes are red and she is yawning. I think she is tired."

words: it is the safe place to cross

title: Diary, invitation and instructions Practice
subject: English
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 English practice on diary, invitation and instructions, from "An Invitation" to "My Diary". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Write an invitation with all the details.
Order the steps in a set of instructions.
Write a personal recount as a diary entry.

guide.what: Different kinds of writing: an invitation, step-by-step instructions and a diary entry.
steps: Look at a real invitation card and find who, what, when and where.
Follow a recipe together and number the steps.
Talk about the day before writing the diary.
home: Make an invitation for a family dinner.
Keep a diary for one week, writing three sentences each night.
guide.watch: A diary uses I and the past tense. Remind your child to say how they felt, not only what they did.

title: Shapes and lines Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on shapes and lines, from "Flat Shapes" to "Straight or Curved?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count sides and corners of 2D shapes.
Name 3D shapes: cube, sphere, cylinder, cone.
Tell straight lines from curved lines.

guide.what: Naming flat and solid shapes and describing them by sides, corners and lines.
steps: Feel a box and count its corners.
Roll a ball and a box: which one rolls?
Look for straight and curved lines in the room.
home: Find a cylinder, a sphere and a cube in the kitchen.
Build towers with boxes and tins.
guide.watch: A cube and a square are different: a cube is solid and has 6 square faces.

title: Money Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on money, from "Pakistani Coins and Notes" to "At the Shop". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recognise Pakistani coins and notes.
Add small amounts of money.
Decide if there is enough money to buy something.

guide.what: Recognising Pakistani rupee coins and notes, adding small amounts and shopping.
steps: Let your child hold and name each coin.
Play shop with real or toy coins.
Count coins starting with the biggest value.
home: Let your child pay at a small shop with your help.
Set up a pretend tuck shop at home.
guide.watch: A bigger coin is not always worth more. Teach the number on it, not the size.

title: Time Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Maths practice on time, from "O'Clock" to "My Day". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell the time to the hour.
Tell the time to the half hour.
Order the times of day.

guide.what: Telling the time to the hour and half hour, and the parts of the day.
steps: Show a real clock: the short hand is the hour, the long hand the minutes.
At o'clock, the long hand points straight up to 12.
At half past, the long hand points straight down to 6.
home: Ask your child to tell you when it is 5 o'clock.
Make a paper plate clock together.
guide.watch: Children mix up the two hands. Say "the short hand is short of time, it moves slowly".

title: My body and senses Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on my body and senses, from "Body Parts" to "Look After Your Body". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name body parts and what they do.
Match actions to the five senses.
Choose healthy habits.

guide.what: Naming body parts and the five senses, and keeping our bodies healthy.
steps: Play "Simon says touch your..."
Do a blindfold taste test with safe foods.
Talk about why we sleep and exercise.
home: Make a daily healthy habits chart.
Go on a sense walk: what can you hear, see and smell?
guide.watch: Children may think the heart is on the left of the chest only. It is in the middle, tilted slightly left.

title: Healthy food Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on healthy food, from "Healthy or Not?" to "Where Does It Come From?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell everyday healthy foods from treats.
Sort foods into fruits, vegetables and grains.
Know that food comes from plants and animals.

guide.what: Healthy food, food groups and where our food comes from.
steps: Name the foods on your plate and their groups.
Talk about why treats are for sometimes.
Visit a vegetable stall and name everything.
home: Let your child help pack a healthy lunch.
Grow a small plant like mint or coriander.
guide.watch: Avoid calling foods "good" or "bad". Say "everyday foods" and "sometimes foods".

title: Materials around us Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Science practice on materials around us, from "What Is It Made Of?" to "Floats or Sinks?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name common materials.
Describe materials as hard or soft.
Predict and test if things float or sink.

guide.what: Things are made of materials like wood, metal, glass, plastic and cloth, each with its own properties.
steps: Touch things and describe them: hard, soft, smooth, rough.
Ask: Why is a window made of glass?
Test things in a tub of water.
home: Sort kitchen things by material.
Make a float or sink chart.
guide.watch: A heavy ship floats because of its shape. For now, just test and talk about what happens.

title: My school Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on my school, from "People at School" to "All About My School". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name people who work at school.
Know and follow school rules.
Write about your own school.

guide.what: The people at school, school rules and our own school.
steps: Talk about your child's school day: who did you meet?
Ask why each school rule matters.
Say thank you to school staff together.
home: Make a card for a teacher or the school guard.
Pack the school bag together the night before.
guide.watch: Some children feel shy at school. Ask about one happy moment each day.

title: Community helpers Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on community helpers, from "Who Helps Us?" to "Thank You, Helpers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name community helpers.
Match helpers to their workplaces.
Know when to call for help.

guide.what: People in the community who help us, where they work and how to ask for help.
steps: Point out helpers when you are out: the sweeper, the traffic warden.
Ask: What would happen without farmers?
Learn emergency numbers together.
home: Role play being a doctor or shopkeeper.
Give a cold drink to a worker on a hot day.
guide.watch: Every job deserves respect. Talk about sweepers and cleaners as important helpers too.

title: Pakistan, my country Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Social Studies practice on pakistan, my country, from "National Symbols" to "Our Leaders". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the national symbols of Pakistan.
Know Pakistan's national days.
Know the founders of Pakistan.

guide.what: Pakistan's national symbols, national days and founders.
steps: Show the national symbols on a poster or online.
Talk about why we celebrate 14 August.
Find Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad on a map.
home: Learn a national song.
Visit Minar-e-Pakistan, Mazar-e-Quaid or Faisal Mosque if you can.
guide.watch: Keep history simple at this age: Pakistan was made so people could live freely.

title: واحد اور جمع کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on one and many (واحد اور جمع), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Write simple Urdu plurals.
Tell singular from plural.
Use singular and plural in sentences.

guide.what: Singular and plural words in Urdu.
steps: Count objects and say one or many in Urdu.
Show patterns: ا becomes ے, ی becomes یاں.
Play "ایک یا بہت" with toys.
home: Count fruit at the market in Urdu.
Make word cards for singular and plural pairs.
guide.watch: Some words stay the same (درخت، پھول). Learn them as special words.

title: نظم: بچے کی دعا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on poem: a child's prayer (نظم: بچے کی دعا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and recite a famous Urdu poem.
Learn meanings of words in the poem.
Find opposites from the poem.

guide.what: Reading and reciting Allama Iqbal's poem "Bachay ki Dua" and learning its words.
steps: Recite the poem together each morning.
Explain each hard word with an example.
Talk about how a candle gives light to others.
home: Learn the first two couplets by heart.
Light a candle and talk about the meaning.
guide.watch: Many schools recite this poem in assembly. Knowing it well builds confidence.

title: کہانی پڑھیں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Urdu practice on reading a story (کہانی پڑھیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Answer questions about a story in one word.
Check facts in a story.
Order the events of a story.

guide.what: Reading a short Urdu story and answering questions about it.
steps: Read the story aloud together.
Ask: کیا، کون، کہاں؟
Retell the story in three steps.
home: Read an Urdu story book at bedtime.
Act out the story with stones and a glass of water.
guide.watch: This is a story of thinking hard. Ask your child what they would have done.

title: Numbers in order Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on numbers in order, from "Count and Write" to "Before and After". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Count objects to 10 and write the number.
Say and write numbers 1 to 10 in order.
Find the number just before and just after.

guide.what: Counting objects to 10 and saying numbers in the right order.
steps: Count stairs, buttons or rotis, touching each one.
Count forwards and backwards from 10 like a rocket launch.
Ask: What comes after 4?
home: Count the cars on the road on the way to school.
Play hopscotch with numbers 1 to 10.
guide.watch: Children often skip or repeat numbers when counting. Touching each object once fixes this.

title: Sorting and matching Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on sorting and matching, from "More or Fewer?" to "Sort by Colour". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare two groups and find the one with more.
See when two groups have the same number.
Sort things into groups.

guide.what: Sorting things into groups and comparing groups to see which has more.
steps: Sort laundry: socks in one pile, shirts in another.
Line up two groups side by side to see which is longer.
Use words: more, fewer, the same.
home: Sort buttons or blocks by colour and size.
Share sweets equally and check both have the same.
guide.watch: Bigger objects can look like "more". Line them up one-to-one to check.

title: Long, short, heavy, light Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Maths practice on long, short, heavy, light, from "Long or Short?" to "Heavy or Light?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare length using long and short.
Compare height using tall and short.
Compare weight using heavy and light.

guide.what: Comparing things by length, height and weight.
steps: Hold two things and ask: Which is heavier?
Line up pencils from short to long.
Stand back to back and see who is taller.
home: Weigh fruit at the market with your hands first, then the scale.
Measure your child against a door frame.
guide.watch: Big things are not always heavy (a balloon). Let your child feel the weight.

title: Fruits and vegetables Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on fruits and vegetables, from "Fruit or Vegetable?" to "My Favourite". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell fruits from vegetables.
Name the colours of fruits and vegetables.
Draw and talk about food.

guide.what: Naming fruits and vegetables and their colours.
steps: Take your child to the fruit and vegetable stall and name everything.
Let your child touch, smell and taste.
Sort fruits and vegetables at home.
home: Make a fruit chaat together.
Play "I spy something yellow" in the kitchen.
guide.watch: Tomatoes are really a fruit, but we cook them like vegetables. Either answer is fine at this age.

title: My home Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on my home, from "Rooms of the House" to "My Family". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name rooms of a house.
Match objects to rooms.
Draw and talk about home and family.

guide.what: Rooms of a house, things in them, and the people who live at home.
steps: Walk around the house and name each room.
Ask: What do we do in the kitchen?
Talk about who lives in your home.
home: Let your child help tidy one room.
Play house with toys.
guide.watch: Homes are different. Some families share rooms. Talk about your home without comparing.

title: Transport Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of Nursery General Knowledge practice on transport, from "Land, Water or Air?" to "Draw a Ride". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort transport by land, water and air.
Count wheels on vehicles.
Draw and talk about transport.

guide.what: Ways we travel on land, water and in the air.
steps: Name vehicles you see on the road.
Count wheels on cars, bikes and rickshaws.
Talk about road safety: hold hands when crossing.
home: Play "stop and go" with red and green cards.
Make a boat from paper and float it.
guide.watch: Every trip is a chance to talk about safety: seatbelts, helmets and holding hands.

title: حروف اور تصویریں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on letters and pictures (حروف اور تصویریں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Hear the first letter of Urdu words.
Match letters to words that start with them.
Trace Urdu letters and say their sounds.

guide.what: Hearing the first letter of Urdu words and matching letters to pictures.
steps: Say the word slowly and stress the first sound.
Show a real object for each letter.
Trace the letter with a finger, then a pencil.
home: Play I Spy in Urdu: "میں ایک چیز دیکھ رہا ہوں جو ب سے شروع ہوتی ہے".
Make a letter book with drawings.
guide.watch: Some letters sound alike (س، ص، ث). At this age, teach the most common one first.

title: رنگ اور گنتی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on colours and counting (رنگ اور گنتی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Name colours in Urdu.
Know the colours of everyday things in Urdu.
Say and write Urdu numbers 1 to 5.

guide.what: Colours and counting from one to five in Urdu.
steps: Name colours in Urdu during the day.
Count steps in Urdu: ایک، دو، تین.
Match colour cards to things at home.
home: Sort clothes by colour and name them in Urdu.
Count rotis at dinner in Urdu.
guide.watch: Many families mix Urdu and English colour names. Both are fine; repeat the Urdu word often.

title: ننھی نظمیں کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Nursery Urdu practice on little rhymes (ننھی نظمیں), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Recite a traditional Urdu rhyme.
Hear Urdu rhyming words.
Draw a picture for a rhyme.

guide.what: Saying traditional Urdu rhymes and hearing words that rhyme.
steps: Say the rhyme with hand actions.
Pause and let your child finish the line.
Clap the beat together.
home: Sing the rhyme at bath time.
Make up a rhyme about your cat or bird.
guide.watch: Rhymes build listening skills for reading Urdu. Repeat them many times.

title: Adding to 10 Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on adding to 10, from "Add the Shapes" to "Make 10". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add two small groups by counting.
Solve simple addition stories.
Find pairs that make 10.

guide.what: Putting two groups together and counting all of them to add.
steps: Use real things: 3 spoons and 2 spoons, how many?
Say the sum as a sentence: 3 and 2 make 5.
Use fingers to make 10.
home: Add plates while setting the dastarkhwan.
Play dice games and add the dots.
guide.watch: Children may count everything from 1 each time. Show them to start from the bigger number and count on.

title: Taking away Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on taking away, from "Take Away" to "Add or Take Away?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Take away from a small group.
Solve simple take-away stories.
Choose whether a story needs adding or taking away.

guide.what: Taking away means some go, and we count how many are left.
steps: Act it out: 5 toys, hide 2, how many are left?
Say: 5 take away 2 leaves 3.
Use "left" and "fewer" in everyday talk.
home: Count rotis before and after dinner.
Sing "Five Little Ducks" and take one away each verse.
guide.watch: The minus sign is new. Call it "take away" until your child is confident.

title: Shapes all around Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of KG Maths practice on shapes all around, from "Name the Shape" to "Count the Sides". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name flat shapes.
Find shapes in everyday objects.
Count the sides of flat shapes.

guide.what: Naming flat shapes, finding them around us and counting their sides.
steps: Go on a shape walk around the house.
Trace the sides of a shape with a finger and count.
Make shapes with sticks or straws.
home: Cut sandwiches into triangles and squares.
Draw pictures using only shapes.
guide.watch: A square is a special rectangle. At this age, just notice that a square's sides are all the same.

title: Healthy habits and safety Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on healthy habits and safety, from "Healthy Habits" to "Emergency Numbers". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose healthy habits.
Know simple safety rules.
Know who to call in an emergency.

guide.what: Healthy habits and simple safety rules at home and outside.
steps: Make hand washing fun: sing while you scrub for 20 seconds.
Practise crossing the road: stop, look, listen.
Learn emergency numbers by heart.
home: Make a bedtime routine chart.
Role play: what to do if you get lost in a market.
guide.watch: Teach "safe strangers": a police officer or a shopkeeper at the counter.

title: Animals and their young Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on animals and their young, from "Baby Animals" to "Pet or Wild?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name baby animals.
Match animals to their homes.
Tell pets from wild animals.

guide.what: Baby animals, animal homes, and pets and wild animals.
steps: Look at animals at a farm or zoo and name their babies.
Talk about how to be gentle with pets.
Read an animal picture book.
home: Visit a nearby farm or park with ducks.
Feed birds on the roof with grain and water.
guide.watch: Many animal babies have special names. A few just add "baby", and that is fine too.

title: Our country Pakistan Practice
subject: General Knowledge
desc: 3 pages of KG General Knowledge practice on our country pakistan, from "Our Flag" to "Our Hero". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the flag of Pakistan.
Know simple facts about Pakistan.
Know who founded Pakistan.

guide.what: Simple facts about Pakistan: the flag, capital, language, national symbols and heroes.
steps: Look at the flag together and name its colours and shapes.
Sing the national anthem or a national song.
Show Pakistan on a map or globe.
home: Decorate your home on 14 August.
Find the flag on coins and notes.
guide.watch: Children enjoy national symbols. Keep facts short and add one new fact a week.

title: زبر، زیر، پیش کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on short vowel marks (زبر، زیر، پیش), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Recognise zabar, zer and pesh.
Read two-letter words with vowel marks.
Choose words with the right vowel marks.

guide.what: The short vowel marks زبر، زیر and پیش and how they change the sound.
steps: Show zabar as a little line above: mouth opens wide.
Zer is a line below: smile.
Pesh is like a small و above: round lips.
home: Move your hand up for zabar, down for zer and forward for pesh.
Read short words on shop signs together.
guide.watch: Most Urdu books drop vowel marks later. Children need them while learning, so keep them in.

title: نظم: ہماری گائے کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on poem: our cow (نظم: ہماری گائے), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a classic Urdu poem for children.
Know what we get from a cow.
Find rhyming words in a poem.

guide.what: Reading a classic poem by Ismail Merathi and talking about what a cow gives us.
steps: Read the poem aloud and let your child repeat each line.
Talk about milk, yogurt and butter.
Find the rhyming words.
home: Visit a dairy or farm.
Make lassi together and talk about where milk comes from.
guide.watch: Ismail Merathi wrote many poems for children over a hundred years ago. They are still loved today.

title: جملے پڑھنا کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of KG Urdu practice on reading sentences (جملے پڑھنا), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read short Urdu sentences.
Complete simple Urdu sentences.
Copy a short Urdu sentence.

guide.what: Reading and writing short Urdu sentences.
steps: Point to each word as you read together.
Ask a simple question after each sentence.
Praise neat letters and spaces.
home: Write a short Urdu note for your child each day.
Read Urdu signs in the market.
guide.watch: Joining letters is the hardest part. Let your child read aloud before writing.

title: Money and shopping Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on money and shopping, from "Count the Money" to "Bazaar Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Add Pakistani money up to Rs 1000.
Work out change by subtracting.
Solve money word problems.

guide.what: Adding money, working out change and solving shopping problems with rupees.
steps: Count money from the biggest note to the smallest.
Count up to find change: 70 + 30 = 100.
Write money with Rs before the number.
home: Let your child check the bill at a shop.
Give a small budget for the tuck shop and plan spending.
guide.watch: Adding money is just adding numbers. Remind your child to line up the digits.

title: Time and calendar Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on time and calendar, from "Quarter Past and To" to "Reading a Calendar". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell the time to the quarter hour.
Know facts about time.
Read days and months on a calendar.

guide.what: Telling the time to the quarter hour and reading a calendar.
steps: At quarter past, the long hand points to 3. At quarter to, it points to 9.
Count in fives around the clock.
Find important dates on a wall calendar.
home: Ask your child to tell you the time each evening.
Mark birthdays and holidays on a calendar.
guide.watch: "Quarter to" is tricky because the hour has not come yet. Practise with a real clock.

title: Length, mass and capacity Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Maths practice on length, mass and capacity, from "Which Unit?" to "Heavier or Lighter?". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Choose metres, kilograms or litres.
Compare measurements.
Compare mass.

guide.what: Measuring length in metres, mass in kilograms and capacity in litres.
steps: Measure a room with a measuring tape.
Read the kg on packets of rice and flour.
Fill a bottle with water and count the litres.
home: Weigh fruit together at the shop.
Measure your height every month.
guide.watch: Big does not always mean heavy. Let your child hold things to compare.

title: Food and teeth Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on food and teeth, from "Food Groups" to "A Balanced Meal". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort foods into energy, body-building and protective foods.
Name types of teeth and care for them.
Choose a balanced meal.

guide.what: Food groups, a balanced diet and how to look after our teeth.
steps: Look at a meal and name each food group.
Look in a mirror and find the different teeth.
Brush teeth together for two minutes.
home: Plan a balanced meal for the family together.
Make a brushing chart with stickers.
guide.watch: Milk teeth fall out from about age 6. It is normal, and the new teeth need extra care.

title: Water Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on water, from "Uses of Water" to "Save Water". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know how we use water.
Describe the water cycle in steps.
Choose ways to save water.

guide.what: How we use water, the water cycle and why we must save water.
steps: Boil water and watch steam rise, then cool on a lid.
Count the ways your family uses water in a day.
Talk about why Pakistan needs to save water.
home: Put a bucket under the AC drain and use the water for plants.
Make a "save water" sign for the bathroom.
guide.watch: Children think clouds are smoke or cotton. Explain they are tiny drops of water.

title: Earth and sky Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Science practice on earth and sky, from "Day and Night" to "Shapes of the Moon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know what we see in the day and night sky.
Know simple facts about the Sun, Moon and Earth.
Notice that the Moon seems to change shape.

guide.what: The Sun, Moon and Earth, day and night, and the changing shape of the Moon.
steps: Shine a torch on a ball in a dark room and turn the ball slowly.
Go out at night and look at the Moon together.
Never look straight at the Sun.
home: Keep a Moon diary for a week.
Watch the sunrise or sunset together.
guide.watch: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight falls on it.

title: Then and now Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on then and now, from "Past or Present?" to "Ask an Elder". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare life in the past and today.
Order events on a timeline.
Learn about the past from older people.

guide.what: How life has changed over time, timelines, and learning history from elders.
steps: Look at old family photos together.
Draw a timeline of your child's life with photos.
Ask grandparents about their childhood.
home: Visit a museum such as Lahore Museum.
Find an old object at home and talk about it.
guide.watch: Children often think "long ago" means dinosaurs. Use family timelines to show recent history.

title: Quaid-e-Azam Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 History practice on quaid-e-azam, from "Life of the Quaid" to "Order the Events". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recall key facts about Quaid-e-Azam.
Understand the Quaid's motto.
Order events in the Quaid's life.

guide.what: The life of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan, and his motto.
steps: Show a photo of the Quaid and talk about his life.
Discuss how the motto can be used at school.
Visit or look at pictures of Mazar-e-Quaid.
home: Celebrate 25 December with a story about the Quaid.
Make a poster of Unity, Faith, Discipline.
guide.watch: Keep it positive: he worked very hard and never gave up.

title: Cities and landmarks Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on cities and landmarks, from "Which City?" to "Port City". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know famous landmarks of Pakistan's cities.
Know the capital of Pakistan and its provinces.
Know facts about Pakistan's cities.

guide.what: Famous cities and landmarks of Pakistan and the capitals of its provinces.
steps: Find each city on a map of Pakistan.
Look at photos of the landmarks together.
Talk about any city your family has visited.
home: Plan a pretend trip around Pakistan.
Make postcards of landmarks.
guide.watch: Karachi is the biggest city, but Islamabad is the capital. Children often mix these up.

title: Seasons in Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Geography practice on seasons in pakistan, from "Four Seasons" to "Hot and Cold Places". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know Pakistan's seasons.
Match clothes and activities to seasons.
Know that weather is different in different places.

guide.what: Pakistan's seasons and how weather changes from place to place.
steps: Talk about this season's weather and clothes.
Watch the weather forecast together.
Compare the weather in two cities.
home: Keep a weather chart for a week.
Collect leaves in autumn.
guide.watch: Seasons vary in Pakistan. The north gets snow while the south stays warm.

title: Villages and cities Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on villages and cities, from "Village or City?" to "Where I Live". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Compare village and city life.
Know jobs in villages and cities.
Describe your own village or city.

guide.what: How life in villages and cities is different and how they depend on each other.
steps: Look at photos of a village and a city and compare.
Ask: Where does our wheat and milk come from?
Talk about relatives who live in a village or city.
home: Visit a village or farm if you can.
Make a two-column list: village, city.
guide.watch: Villages and cities need each other: food comes from villages, many goods come from cities.

title: Rights and responsibilities Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on rights and responsibilities, from "Rights" to "Good Citizens". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know children's basic rights.
Know our responsibilities at home, school and in the community.
Explain how to be a good citizen.

guide.what: Rights are things everyone should have; responsibilities are things we should do.
steps: Talk about one right and one responsibility each day.
Give your child a small household responsibility.
Praise responsible choices.
home: Clean up a park or street with the family.
Make a family rules and responsibilities chart.
guide.watch: Rights and responsibilities go together. Ask: If you have a right to a clean park, what is your responsibility?

title: Festivals of Pakistan Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Social Studies practice on festivals of pakistan, from "Which Festival?" to "My Favourite Festival". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the main festivals in Pakistan.
Recall facts about festivals.
Describe a festival you celebrate.

guide.what: The religious and national festivals celebrated in Pakistan, and respect for all faiths.
steps: Talk about how your family celebrates Eid.
Learn how friends of other faiths celebrate their festivals.
Make Eid cards together.
home: Help prepare a festival dish.
Wish neighbours on their festivals.
guide.watch: Pakistan has people of many faiths. Learning about all festivals builds respect.

title: فہمِ عبارت کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on reading for meaning (فہمِ عبارت), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Answer questions in full Urdu sentences.
Check facts in a passage.
Write about your own experience.

guide.what: Reading an Urdu passage and answering questions in full sentences.
steps: Read the questions first, then the passage.
Underline the answer in the passage.
Start the answer with words from the question.
home: Read an Urdu children's magazine together.
Ask your child to tell you about their day in Urdu.
guide.watch: Full-sentence answers are a new skill. Show how to reuse the question's words.

words: ابو نے زینب کو عیدی دی۔
نانی نے شیر خرما بنایا تھا۔

title: نظم: ایک گائے اور بکری کی مشق
en: Poem: A Cow and a Goat practice
topicEn: Poem: A Cow and a Goat
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on poem: a cow and a goat (نظم: ایک گائے اور بکری), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read a classic Urdu poem.
Learn the meanings of words in the poem.
Find rhyming words.

guide.what: Reading the opening of Iqbal's poem "Aik Gaye aur Bakri" and learning new words.
steps: Read the lines slowly and explain each word.
Look at a picture of a green meadow.
Find the rhyming words at the end of the lines.
home: Read the whole poem from an Iqbal children's book.
Visit a park and describe it in Urdu.
guide.watch: This poem has a lesson about being thankful. Read it all together over a week.

title: جملے اور کہانی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Urdu practice on sentences and stories (جملے اور کہانی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Make sentences with Urdu words.
Order words to make a sentence.
Write a short story from word prompts.

guide.what: Making sentences and writing a short story in Urdu.
steps: Say the sentence aloud before writing.
Check that each sentence ends with ۔
Use first, then, at the end: پہلے، پھر، آخر میں.
home: Tell a story together in Urdu at bedtime.
Write a short Urdu diary entry once a week.
guide.watch: Spelling mistakes are normal. Praise complete sentences and good ideas first.

title: Measurement Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on measurement, from "Units of Length" to "Measurement Problems". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Convert between metres and centimetres.
Convert grams and kilograms, millilitres and litres.
Solve word problems with measurements.

guide.what: Converting between units of length, mass and capacity, and solving measurement problems.
steps: Show 1 metre with a tape and count 100 cm.
Read grams and millilitres on food packets.
Use a measuring jug while cooking.
home: Measure ingredients together for a recipe.
Check the distance to school on a map app.
guide.watch: Children forget to change units before adding. Ask: Are both in metres?

title: Data handling Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on data handling, from "Pictograph" to "Bar Graph Questions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Read a pictograph with a key.
Read and make tally charts.
Answer questions from a data table.

guide.what: Reading and making pictographs, tally charts and simple tables.
steps: Make a tally of birds you see from the window.
Draw a pictograph with a key: each picture equals 2.
Ask questions: most, fewest, how many more?
home: Survey the family about favourite foods and make a chart.
Count cars by colour on a drive.
guide.watch: With a key, each picture may stand for more than one. Always read the key first.

title: Angles and perimeter Practice
subject: Maths
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Maths practice on angles and perimeter, from "Right Angles" to "Lines". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recognise right angles.
Find the perimeter of shapes.
Know horizontal, vertical and parallel lines.

guide.what: Right angles, kinds of lines and finding the perimeter of shapes.
steps: Use the corner of a paper as a right angle checker.
Walk around a table and count the sides.
Look for parallel lines on railway tracks or notebook lines.
home: Measure the perimeter of a photo frame.
Find right angles around the house.
guide.watch: Perimeter is the distance around; area is the space inside. Use a fence and grass to explain.

title: Life cycles Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on life cycles, from "Butterfly Life Cycle" to "Plant Life Cycle". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Order the stages of a butterfly's life cycle.
Describe the life cycle of a frog.
Describe the life cycle of a flowering plant.

guide.what: Living things are born, grow, reproduce and die. Different living things have different life cycles.
steps: Grow a bean in a glass jar and watch each day.
Look at photos of yourself as a baby, toddler and now.
Compare animal babies with their parents.
home: Find a caterpillar on a plant and check on it.
Plant seeds from a fruit you ate.
guide.watch: Some young look like their parents (kittens); others do not (tadpoles). Talk about both.

title: Natural resources Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on natural resources, from "Natural or Man-made?" to "Pollution". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell natural resources from man-made things.
Know the 3 Rs.
Know types of pollution and how to reduce them.

guide.what: Natural resources like water, air, soil and wood, pollution, and the 3 Rs.
steps: Make a list of natural resources you used today.
Sort household waste into paper, plastic and food.
Talk about smog in winter and why it happens.
home: Plant a tree for your birthday.
Make a toy from boxes and bottles.
guide.watch: Recycling is good, but reducing is best. Start with saying no to extra plastic bags.

title: The Sun and shadows Practice
subject: Science
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Science practice on the sun and shadows, from "The Solar System" to "Directions". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know simple facts about the solar system.
Explain how shadows form and change.
Know the four cardinal directions.

guide.what: The Sun and the solar system, how shadows change through the day, and the four directions.
steps: Mark your shadow with chalk in the morning and at noon.
Use a torch and a toy to make shadows.
Find east by watching the sunrise.
home: Make a model of the solar system with fruits of different sizes.
Use a compass app to find north.
guide.watch: The Sun does not really move across the sky; the Earth spins. Explain with a torch and a ball.

title: Allama Iqbal Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on allama iqbal, from "Life of Iqbal" to "The Falcon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recall key facts about Allama Iqbal.
Understand Iqbal's role in the Pakistan Movement.
Understand an idea from Iqbal's poetry.

guide.what: The life and ideas of Allama Muhammad Iqbal, the national poet of Pakistan.
steps: Recite "Lab pe aati hai dua" together.
Find Sialkot and Lahore on a map.
Talk about what being like a shaheen means.
home: Listen to a children's poem by Iqbal.
Visit or look at pictures of Iqbal's tomb.
guide.watch: Iqbal wrote in Urdu and Persian. Children can enjoy his simple poems first.

title: The Pakistan Movement Practice
subject: History
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 History practice on the pakistan movement, from "Key Events" to "Leaders of the Movement". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know key dates of the Pakistan Movement.
Understand the Pakistan Resolution.
Know leaders of the Pakistan Movement.

guide.what: The main events and leaders of the Pakistan Movement, from 1906 to 1947.
steps: Draw a timeline from 1906 to 1947.
Look at pictures of Minar-e-Pakistan.
Talk about why people wanted a new country.
home: Watch the Pakistan Day parade on TV.
Make a flag and a timeline poster.
guide.watch: History is about people. Focus on leaders' hard work and teamwork, not just dates.

title: Rivers of Pakistan Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on rivers of pakistan, from "The Indus River" to "Why Rivers Matter". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know facts about the Indus River.
Name the rivers of Punjab.
Explain the importance of rivers.

guide.what: The Indus and the rivers of Punjab, and why rivers matter to Pakistan.
steps: Trace the Indus on a map from north to south.
Talk about dams and why we need them.
Count the five rivers on your fingers.
home: Visit a river or canal bank with the family.
Find out which river is closest to your city.
guide.watch: The Beas mostly flows in India today, but it is still one of Punjab's five rivers.

title: Crops and resources Practice
subject: Geography
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Geography practice on crops and resources, from "Crops of Pakistan" to "Uses of Resources". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know major crops and their seasons.
Know where key natural resources are found in Pakistan.
Know how resources are used.

guide.what: Pakistan's main crops, natural resources and how we use them.
steps: Look at food packets and find what they are made from.
Talk about where the gas for the stove comes from.
Find Sui, Khewra and Thar on a map.
home: Visit a farm or a field of wheat.
Buy a piece of pink Khewra salt and look at it.
guide.watch: Rabi crops grow in winter, Kharif crops in summer. Use wheat and rice as the easy examples.

title: Our government Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on our government, from "What Does Government Do?" to "Taxes". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know services the government provides.
Know the federal, provincial and local levels of government.
Understand why people pay taxes.

guide.what: What government does, the levels of government in Pakistan and why taxes matter.
steps: Point out a government service near home: a road, school or hospital.
Explain voting with a family vote on dinner.
Talk about the four provinces.
home: Hold a family election for a weekend activity.
Write a letter to the local council about a problem.
guide.watch: Keep politics out of it. Focus on how government should serve the people.

title: Jobs and professions Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on jobs and professions, from "Who Makes What?" to "When I Grow Up". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name professions and their work.
Tell goods from services.
Describe a profession and why it matters.

guide.what: Different professions, goods and services, and respect for all work.
steps: Ask family members about their jobs.
Notice the jobs people do on a street.
Talk about skills each job needs.
home: Interview a relative about their job.
Visit a craftsperson like a potter or tailor.
guide.watch: Avoid ranking jobs. Every job, from sweeper to surgeon, keeps the country running.

title: Cultures of Pakistan Practice
subject: Social Studies
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Social Studies practice on cultures of pakistan, from "Provinces and Languages" to "Unity in Diversity". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the provinces and main languages of Pakistan.
Know foods, crafts and dress from different regions.
Explain what unites people in Pakistan.

guide.what: The many cultures of Pakistan: provinces, languages, food and dress, and what unites us.
steps: Listen to songs in different Pakistani languages.
Cook a dish from another province.
Find each province on a map.
home: Learn to say hello in a new Pakistani language.
Make a scrapbook of cultures.
guide.watch: Many languages are spoken in each province. These are examples, not the only languages.

title: ضمیر کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on pronouns (ضمیر), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Identify Urdu pronouns.
Use pronouns instead of names.
Sort pronouns by person.

guide.what: Pronouns in Urdu: words used instead of names, like میں، تم، وہ.
steps: Retell a story replacing names with pronouns.
Point to people and say میں، تم، وہ.
Explain that آپ shows respect.
home: Talk about family members using pronouns.
Find pronouns in an Urdu storybook.
guide.watch: آپ is used for elders and for respect. Encourage your child to use it with grown-ups.

title: نظم: ہمدردی کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on poem: kindness (نظم: ہمدردی), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Read and understand a classic Urdu poem.
Understand the message of a poem.
Learn meanings of words in the poem.

guide.what: Reading Iqbal's poem "Hamdardi" and understanding its message of helping others.
steps: Read the poem aloud and tell the story of the firefly.
Discuss: How can we help someone who is lost or sad?
Explain new words with gestures.
home: Do one kind act each day this week.
Read the full poem and draw the firefly.
guide.watch: The full poem is longer. Read it together over a few days and talk about kindness.

title: درخواست اور خط کی مشق
subject: Urdu
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Urdu practice on application and letter (درخواست اور خط), with an answer key for every page.
obj: Complete a leave application in Urdu.
Know the parts of a letter.
Write a short informal letter in Urdu.

guide.what: Writing a leave application and a short letter in Urdu.
steps: Look at a real application and find its parts.
Practise the opening and closing lines.
Talk about polite words: گزارش، شکریہ.
home: Write a real letter to a grandparent and post it.
Write an Eid card in Urdu.
guide.watch: Applications are formal; letters to family are friendly. Compare the two styles.

title: Allah the Creator Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on allah the creator, from "Allah Is One" to "Saying Thank You". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know that Allah is One and the Creator of all.
Name the blessings of Allah.
Use the right words to remember Allah.

guide.what: Allah is One, the Creator of everything, and we thank Him for His blessings.
steps: Name three blessings at dinner each day.
Look at the sky, plants and animals and talk about Allah's creation.
Say Alhamdulillah together after meals.
home: Make a blessings list on the fridge.
Draw a picture of your favourite part of nature.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Wudu and Salah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on wudu and salah, from "Steps of Wudu" to "Salah". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the order of the steps of wudu.
Know simple facts about wudu.
Know simple facts about Salah.

guide.what: The steps of wudu and simple facts about Salah.
steps: Practise the steps of wudu together slowly.
Talk about saving water during wudu.
Show which way the Qibla is at home.
home: Make a wudu steps chart for the bathroom.
Go to the mosque together for Jumu'ah if you can.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook. Small differences in the details of wudu are taught by teachers; follow your child's school book.

title: Islamic months Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Islamiat practice on islamic months, from "Months in Order" to "The Moon". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the Islamic months in order.
Know important events in the Islamic year.
Know that Islamic months follow the moon.

guide.what: The twelve Islamic months and the special events in them.
steps: Look at an Islamic calendar together.
Find this month's name in the Islamic calendar.
Look for the new moon at the start of a month.
home: Mark Ramadan and the two Eids on a calendar.
Learn three month names a week.
guide.watch: Islamic months follow the moon, so Ramadan and Eid come about 10 or 11 days earlier each year.

title: Input and output Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on input and output, from "Input or Output?" to "Storage". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Sort input and output devices.
Explain input and output.
Know where computers store work.

guide.what: Input devices send information in, output devices give it out, and storage keeps it.
steps: Type a letter and watch it appear: input then output.
Print a drawing together and talk about output.
Record your voice with the microphone.
home: Make an input and output poster.
Find input and output devices on a phone.
guide.watch: A touchscreen is both input and output. That is a great question for curious children.

title: The desktop Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on the desktop, from "Desktop Words" to "Save Your Work". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know parts of the computer desktop.
Shut down a computer correctly.
Know why we save work.

guide.what: Parts of the desktop, saving work and shutting down a computer correctly.
steps: Show the icons, taskbar and folders on your computer.
Make a folder with your child's name.
Practise saving a drawing.
home: Make a desktop picture on paper with icons.
Practise shutting down properly.
guide.watch: Different computers look a little different. Teach the idea, not one exact screen.

words: a small picture for a program
a box where a program opens

title: Staying safe online Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 2 Computer practice on staying safe online, from "Safe or Not Safe?" to "If Something Feels Wrong". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Make safe choices online.
Know what information to keep private.
Know what to do if something online feels wrong.

guide.what: Keeping personal information private and asking a grown-up for help online.
steps: Agree on family internet rules.
Use devices in a shared room.
Tell your child they will never be in trouble for telling you.
home: Make a family online rules poster.
Practise saying "I will ask a grown-up first".
guide.watch: Children should feel safe telling you anything. Stay calm when they share something worrying.

title: The Holy Quran Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on the holy quran, from "Quran Facts" to "Holy Books". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know basic facts about the Holy Quran.
Show respect for the Holy Quran.
Know the holy books revealed by Allah.

guide.what: Basic facts about the Holy Quran, respecting it, and the holy books revealed by Allah.
steps: Show your child where the Quran is kept at home and why.
Count the paras and surahs together in a mushaf.
Talk about how the Quran was revealed.
home: Listen to a short surah together each day.
Read the Quran with a qualified teacher.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Prophets of Allah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on prophets of allah, from "First and Last" to "What Prophets Taught". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know the first and last prophets.
Know a famous event from the life of some prophets.
Know what all prophets taught.

guide.what: Prophets of Allah, the first and last prophets, and famous events from their lives.
steps: Read a prophet story from a children's Islamiat book.
Talk about what each prophet teaches us.
Say (AS) and (PBUH) after their names.
home: Make a prophets timeline from Hazrat Adam (AS) to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Draw the ark of Hazrat Nuh (AS).
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Islamiat practice on life of the holy prophet (pbuh), from "Early Life" to "His Good Qualities". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know facts about the early life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
Know about the Hijrah to Madinah.
Learn the good qualities of the Holy Prophet (PBUH).

guide.what: The early life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH), the Hijrah and his good qualities.
steps: Read a seerah story from your child's Islamiat book.
Pick one good quality and practise it for a week.
Find Makkah and Madinah on a map.
home: Make a good qualities chart and tick it daily.
Ask your child to retell one seerah story.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Hardware and software Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on hardware and software, from "Hardware or Software?" to "Computer Jobs". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Tell hardware from software.
Define hardware, software and programs.
Choose the right software for a job.

guide.what: Hardware is what we can touch; software is the set of instructions that makes it work.
steps: Point to hardware and open software on your computer.
Talk about which app you use for which job.
Explain that apps on a phone are software too.
home: Make a hardware and software sorting game.
Try a new learning app together.
guide.watch: The operating system is the big program that runs all the others. Use a phone as an example.

title: Typing and documents Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on typing and documents, from "Word Processor Words" to "Home Row". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know word processing words.
Use common keyboard shortcuts.
Know the home row for typing.

guide.what: Word processing, formatting and keyboard shortcuts, and the home row keys for typing.
steps: Type a short paragraph and make one word bold.
Find the bumps on F and J.
Practise one shortcut each day.
home: Type a birthday card for a relative.
Use a free typing game for 10 minutes.
guide.watch: Correct finger placement now saves bad habits later. Short practice is best.

title: The internet Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 3 Computer practice on the internet, from "Internet Words" to "Being Kind Online". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know internet words.
Choose strong passwords.
Be a good digital citizen.

guide.what: Using the internet: browsers, search engines, strong passwords and being kind online.
steps: Search for a school topic together and compare two sites.
Make a strong password together using a fun phrase.
Talk about kind and unkind messages.
home: Write family rules for messaging apps.
Find an answer online and check it in a book.
guide.watch: Children believe what they read online. Teach them to ask "Who wrote this and how do they know?"

title: Kalima and Bismillah Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on kalima and bismillah, from "Kalima Tayyiba" to "Allah's Gifts". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Recite the Kalima Tayyiba and know its meaning.
Know Bismillah, its meaning and when we say it.
Know that Allah is the Creator of everything.

guide.what: The Kalima Tayyiba and Bismillah, their meanings, and Allah as the Creator.
steps: Say Bismillah together before meals.
Recite the Kalima slowly, one part at a time.
Look at nature and talk about Allah's creation.
home: Make Bismillah a family habit before eating and starting homework.
Go for a walk and name things Allah created.
guide.watch: Learn the Arabic words and their correct recitation from your child's Islamiat teacher and school textbook.

title: Pillars of Islam Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on pillars of islam, from "Five Pillars" to "Ramadan". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the five pillars of Islam.
Name the five daily prayers and their times.
Know simple facts about fasting in Ramadan.

guide.what: The five pillars of Islam and the five daily prayers.
steps: Count the five pillars on one hand.
Point to the sky at each prayer time and name it.
Talk about what your family does in Ramadan.
home: Make a five pillars hand print poster.
Listen for the azan and name the prayer.
guide.watch: Sehri is the meal before dawn and Iftar is the meal at sunset. Children often mix them up.

title: Good manners Practice
subject: Islamiat
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Islamiat practice on good manners, from "Greetings" to "My Good Deed". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Use Islamic greetings and good words.
Choose good manners.
Reflect on good deeds.

guide.what: Islamic greetings and good manners at home, school and with others.
steps: Greet family members with Assalam o Alaikum every morning.
Praise your child when they use good words.
Talk about kindness to neighbours.
home: Keep a good deeds jar: add a bead for each kind act.
Practise saying JazakAllah when someone helps.
guide.watch: Children learn manners by watching. Use these words yourself every day.

title: Parts of a computer Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on parts of a computer, from "Name the Parts" to "Computer Words". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Name the main parts of a computer.
Find computers around us.
Use basic computer words.

guide.what: The main parts of a computer and computers we see around us.
steps: Point to each part of a computer or laptop and name it.
Talk about devices at home that have a computer inside.
Let your child press the power button with you.
home: Draw and label a computer.
Look for screens and buttons on machines when you go out.
guide.watch: A laptop has the same parts as a desktop, just joined together. Point them out.

title: Mouse and keyboard Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on mouse and keyboard, from "Mouse Actions" to "Sit Right". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know mouse actions.
Know special keys on the keyboard.
Use a computer safely and comfortably.

guide.what: Using the mouse and keyboard, and sitting correctly at a computer.
steps: Let your child practise clicking and dragging in a drawing app.
Show the space bar, enter and backspace keys.
Set a timer for short screen sessions.
home: Type your child's name together.
Play a simple mouse game together.
guide.watch: Small hands may find a big mouse hard. A touchpad or small mouse helps.

words: move up and down the page

title: Using computers Practice
subject: Computer
desc: 3 pages of Grade 1 Computer practice on using computers, from "What Can We Do?" to "Draw a Computer". An answer key for every page is at the back.
obj: Know uses of computers.
Know healthy screen habits.
Draw and label a computer.

guide.what: What we can do with computers and healthy screen habits.
steps: Show your child two things you use a computer for at work or home.
Agree on simple screen time rules.
Praise your child for asking before using a device.
home: Use a paint program together.
Make a screen time chart.
guide.watch: Screens are useful, but play, books and sleep come first at this age.
